idiom_name: decorator registration + duck-typed callables (Flask routes, pytest fixtures)
implementation_notes: Python inverts control with function values and naming conventions rather than base classes: @app.route registers a view function that the WSGI application calls per request, and pytest inspects test signatures, calls the requested fixtures and passes their results into the test. The classic framework skeleton is replaced by registration plus a plain callable (or any object with the expected method), which is the idiomatic default for web handlers and test code. Subclassing remains the clearer contract when the framework documents a component lifecycle with several hooks, such as unittest's setUp/tearDown or Django's AppConfig.ready.
pitfalls: Framework callbacks run in whatever concurrency context the caller owns: Flask handlers and Django views may execute on multiple threads, so module-level mutable state must be synchronised or avoided.
Registration happens at import time, so an exception during import silently removes routes or fixtures; the failure surfaces as a 404 or a missing-fixture error rather than at the definition site.
